body_ar:
تعظيم اسم الله سبحانه وتعالى ووجهه الكريم أن يسأل بهما غير الجنة

ما معنى لا يسأل بوجه الله إلا الجنة؟

هذا نهي من الرسول (ص) عن أن يقول أحد لأحد أسألك بوجه الله أن تقضي لي كذا، بل لا يسأل بوجه الله العظيم إلا الجنة، تقول: اللهم إني أسألك بوجهك العظيم الفردوس الأعلى من الجنة لأنه أمر عظيم فلا يسأل به إلا الجنة، وما ذلك إلا من تعظيم اسم الله سبحانه وتعالى ووجهه الكريم.

----------------------------------------------------

تعليق التمائم و الحروز

ما حكم تعليق التمائم و الحروز؟...

أن التمائم هي ما يتعلقه الإنسان من مثل الكعاب أو الودع أو العظام أو بعض الملابس الخلقة أو الشعر أو نحو ذلك و تعلق كل هذا حرام بل عده النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من الشرك بالله فقال:من تعلق تميمة وكل إليها و قال:من تعلق شيئا وكل إليه و قال أما إنها لا تزيدك إلا وهنا و قال:من تعلق تميمة فلا أتم الله له. و قال:إن الرقى و التمائم و التولة شرك فقد جعلها شركا بالله و حذر منها غاية التحذير

فلذلك على الناس أن يعلموا أنها من أمر الجاهلية و أنها لا خير فيها فالقرون التي يعلقها الناس أو الودع أو نحو ذلك كل هذا من التمائم التي هي من الشرك بالله و على الإنسان أن ينتزعها إذا كانت عليه و أن يقطعها عن أولاده إذا كانوا يتعلقونها أو عن كل من ينصح له من المؤمنين فالناس جميعا إخوانكم يجب على كل إنسان منكم أن يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه فإذا رأىأحدا يتعلق شيئا من ذلك عليه أن ينصحه بأن يقطعه عن نفسه فإنه لا يزيده من الله إلا بعدا

و أما الحروز فهي جمع حرز فهو ما كتب و علق فهذا إن كان من كتاب الله أو من سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم و قصد به الشفاء من مرض محدد فإنه إن كان نظيفا و لم يزد عليه غيره و كتب على صورة كتابه و لم تقطع حروفه و إنما كتب فيه القرآن أو الدعاء النبوي كما هو فيمكن أن يعلق على المريض حتى يبرأ فإذا برء مزق عنه و لم يترك عليه كالمجنون الذي يعلق عليه مثلا آية الكرسي أو غيرها من الآيات أو سورة البقرة بكاملها فيمكن أن يعلق هذا على المجانين أو المرضى فإذا برء وا مزقوه عن أنفسهم و لا يمكن أن يعلق بصفة دائمة أو مستمرة فإن ذلك من عمل الجاهلية.

----------------------------------------------------

تعليق على قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن أبي وأباك في النار»

قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن أبي وأباك في النار» وعبد الله بن عبد المطلب في الفترة؟

أن النبي (ص) ما ينطق عن الهوى وما يقوله لن يقوله إلا بوحي، وقد صح عنه أنه قال للأعرابي إن أبي وأباك في النار فدل هذا على أن الله أخبره بذلك، وليس في هذا نقص للنبي (ص) ولا تقليل من شأنه، فلو كان كذلك لم يمت أبوه قبل مولده، فإن الله لم ينصره بالآباء ولا بالأمهات ولا بالإخوة ولا بالأخوات وإنما نصره بنصره العزيز المكين الذي نصره به وقال فيه: {إنا فتحنا لك فتحا مبينا ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر ويتم نعمته عليك} فأتم الله عليه نعمته ونصره هذا النصر العزيز.

----------------------------------------------------

تقسيمات التوحيد

كنا نعتقد أن التوحيد على ثلاثة أقسام: الواجب في حق الله والمستحيل في حق الله تعالى والجائز في حقه تعالى وكذلك الرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام، وقلتم إن التوحيد على ثلاثة أقسام الإيمان بالألوهية والربوبية وتوحيد الأسماء والصفات، أريد التوفيق بينهما؟

أنه لا مشاحة في الاصطلاح، فالتقسيم الذي ذكرناه هو الحاصل العقلي، والتقسيم الذي ذكره السائل يبين فقط مراتب الصفات، فالصفات من حيث إطلاقها على الله عز وجل تنقسم إلى هذه الأقسام الثلاثة، ما يجب أن يؤمن الإنسان بأن الله متصف به وهو ما أخبر به عن نفسه، وما يجوز فيه ذلك وهو الأفعال الاختيارية كالرزق والإماتة والإحياء وغير ذلك، وما يستحيل وهو النقص والعيب فهذا يستحيل،

أما معرفة ذلك تفصيلا كعد الصفات وحصرها في عدد محدد، أو عد المستحيل وحصره في عدد محدد أو عد الجائز وحصره في عدد محدد فلا دليل عليه.

----------------------------------------------------

تنعم المؤمنات بأزواجهن في الجنة

هل يتنعم المؤمنات بأزواجهن في الجنة و ما هو نعيم من لم يتزوجن من النساء؟

نعم و النساء في الجنة أكثر من الرجال لأنه ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «أنه ما من رجل من أهل الدنيا إلا و أقل نسائه في الجنة اثنتان من نساء الدنيا» كل رجل من رجال الدنيا أقل نسائه في الجنة اثنتان من نساء الدنيا غير الحور العين فلذلك يتمتعن بأزواجهن و يزوجهن الله سبحانه وتعالى و يختار لهن الأزواج من رجال الدنيا و لذلك فإن مريم بنت عمران و ارأة فرعون يزوجهن الله سبحانه وتعالى يوم القيامة محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فيختار لهما من الرجال لأن الله ضربهما مثلا لأهل الإيمان فاختار لهما أكمل أهل الإيمان إيمانا فزوجهما برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم القيامة

و كذلك أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هن أزواجه في الآخرة فقد أمره الله بتخييرهن فمن اختارته اختارت الله و رسوله فتكون زوجة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الآخرة قال الله تعالى: ﴿يأيها النبي قل لأزواجك إن كنتن تردن الحيواة الدنيا و زينتها فتعالين أمتعكن و أسرحكن سراحا جميلا و إن كنتن تردن الله و رسوله و الدار الآخرة فإن الله أعد للمحسنات منكن أجرا عظيما﴾

و قد صح في صحيح البخاري من حديث عمار ابن ياسر رضي الله عنه أنه قال لأهل العراق حين خرجوا مع عائشة رضي الله عنها في وقعة الجمل قال: أما إنها لزوجة نبيكم في الدنيا و الآخرة و لكن الله امتحنكم بها هل تطيعونها أم تطيعونه فهن أزواجه في الآخرة كما هم أزواجه في الدنيا.
body_en:
Magnifying the name of God, glorified and exalted, and His noble face, such that nothing but the Garden is asked by them

What is the meaning of 'nothing is asked by the face of God except the Garden'?

This is a prohibition from the Messenger, upon whom be peace, against anyone saying to another: 'I ask you by the face of God to do such-and-such for me.' Rather, nothing is asked by the mighty face of God except the Garden. You say: 'O God, I ask You by Your mighty face for the highest Firdaws of the Garden' — because it is a mighty thing, so nothing is asked by it but the Garden. And that is only out of magnifying the name of God, glorified and exalted, and His noble face.

----------------------------------------------------

Hanging amulets and written charms

What is the ruling on hanging amulets (tamāʾim) and written charms (ḥurūz)?...

Amulets are what a person hangs on himself, such as knuckle-bones, cowrie shells, bones, pieces of worn-out clothing, hair and the like. Hanging any of this is forbidden (ḥarām); indeed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, counted it as associating partners with God (shirk), for he said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet is consigned to it'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs anything is consigned to it'; and he said: 'Truly it will only increase you in weakness'; and he said: 'Whoever hangs an amulet — may God not bring anything to completion for him'; and he said: 'Incantations, amulets and love-charms are associating partners with God.' So he made them an associating of partners with God and warned against them in the strongest terms.

For that reason people must know that they are of the affairs of the age of ignorance and that there is no good in them. The horns that people hang, or the cowries, or the like — all of this is among the amulets that are an associating of partners with God. A person must tear them off if they are on him, and cut them away from his children if they are wearing them, and from everyone among the believers whom he advises. For all people are your brothers; every one of you is obliged to love for his brother what he loves for himself. So if he sees anyone wearing anything of that, he must advise him to cut it off from himself, for it only increases him in distance from God.

As for ḥurūz, this is the plural of ḥirz, and it is what is written and hung. If this is from the Book of God or from the sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is intended by it that a specified illness be healed — then, provided it is clean, and nothing else has been added to it, and it is written in the form in which it is written, with its letters not broken up, and only the Qur'an or the prophetic supplication is written in it as it stands — then it may be hung on the sick person until he recovers; and when he recovers it is torn off him and not left on him. Like the insane person on whom, for example, the Verse of the Throne is hung, or other verses, or the whole of Sūrat al-Baqarah: this may be hung on the insane or on the sick, and when they recover they tear it off themselves. It cannot be hung permanently or continuously, for that is of the work of the age of ignorance.

----------------------------------------------------

A comment on the Prophet's words, may God bless him and grant him peace: 'My father and your father are in the Fire'

The Prophet's words, may God bless him and grant him peace: 'My father and your father are in the Fire' — and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib was in the interval between the messengers?

The Prophet, upon whom be peace, does not speak from caprice, and what he says he will not say except by revelation. It is soundly established from him that he said to the bedouin: 'My father and your father are in the Fire.' This indicates that God informed him of that. There is in this no deficiency for the Prophet, upon whom be peace, and no lessening of his standing; for had it been so, his father would not have died before his birth. God did not aid him by fathers, nor by mothers, nor by brothers, nor by sisters; rather He aided him with His mighty and firm help, with which He aided him, and concerning which He said: {Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what came after, and complete His favour upon you} (Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:1–2). So God completed His favour upon him and granted him this mighty help.

----------------------------------------------------

The divisions of tawḥīd

We used to believe that tawḥīd is of three divisions: what is necessarily true of God, what is impossible of God, exalted, and what is rationally possible in His case, exalted — and likewise for the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace. And you said that tawḥīd is of three divisions: belief in divinity, and lordship, and the oneness of the names and attributes. I would like the two to be reconciled.

There is no quarrelling over technical terms. The division we mentioned is the rational outcome, and the division the questioner mentioned only sets out the ranks of the attributes. The attributes, as regards their being applied to God, mighty and majestic, divide into these three divisions: what a person must believe that God is described by, which is what He has told about Himself; what is rationally possible in that regard, which is the acts of will, such as providing, causing death, giving life and so on; and what is impossible, which is deficiency and defect — this is impossible.

As for knowing that in detail — such as enumerating the attributes and confining them to a fixed number, or enumerating the impossible and confining it to a fixed number, or enumerating the rationally possible and confining it to a fixed number — there is no evidence for it.

----------------------------------------------------

The enjoyment of believing women with their husbands in the Garden

Will believing women enjoy their husbands in the Garden, and what is the bliss of those women who did not marry?

Yes; and women in the Garden are more numerous than men, because it is established from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that 'there is no man of the people of this world but that the fewest of his wives in the Garden is two of the women of this world.' Every man of the men of this world — the fewest of his wives in the Garden is two of the women of this world, apart from the wide-eyed maidens. So they take delight in their husbands, and God, glorified and exalted, marries them and chooses husbands for them from the men of this world. That is why Mary the daughter of Imran and the wife of Pharaoh — God, glorified and exalted, will marry them on the Day of Resurrection to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He will choose for the two of them from among the men, because God set the two of them as a parable for the people of faith; so He chose for them the most perfect in faith among the people of faith, and married them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Resurrection.

Likewise, the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are his wives in the Hereafter, for God commanded him to give them the choice, and whoever chose him chose God and His Messenger, and so she is the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Hereafter. God, exalted, said: {O Prophet, say to your wives: if you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release. But if you desire God and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter, then truly God has prepared for those of you who do good an immense reward} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:28–29).

It is soundly established in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Ammar ibn Yasir, may God be pleased with him, that he said to the people of Iraq when they had gone out with Aishah, may God be pleased with her, at the Battle of the Camel — he said: 'Truly she is the wife of your Prophet in this world and in the Hereafter, but God has tested you by her: whether you obey her, or obey Him.' So they are his wives in the Hereafter just as they are his wives in this world.

flags.arabic: الواجب في حق الله والمستحيل في حق الله تعالى والجائز في حقه تعالى … ما يجوز فيه ذلك وهو الأفعال الاختيارية … وما يستحيل وهو النقص والعيب
flags.context: the fourth item, on the divisions of tawḥīd
options: necessarily true of God / rationally possible / impossible — the kalām modalities
obligatory / permissible / forbidden — the five legal rulings
flags.note: KALĀM EXEMPTION, style guide §8. This item is the exact case the rule was written for. wājib, jāʾiz and mumtaniʿ/mustaḥīl here are terms of rational modality applied to propositions about God, not legal rulings applied to acts: 'what is necessarily true of God', 'what is rationally possible', 'what is impossible'. Rendering them as 'obligatory', 'permissible' and 'forbidden' would make nonsense of the answer — God would be said to have obligations. One exception inside the same paragraph: ما يجب أن يؤمن الإنسان, 'what a person must believe', attaches to a human act and is a genuine obligation; that clause is rendered accordingly. Flagged rather than left silent because a later reviser working from the glossary alone would very likely get this wrong.

flags.arabic: وعبد الله بن عبد المطلب في الفترة؟ … و ما هو نعيم من لم يتزوجن من النساء؟
flags.context: two parts of two questions on this page that the Sheikh does not answer
options: render the questions in full and leave them unanswered, as the source does
display these items with a note that part of the question is not answered in the written text
withhold the affected items until the Sheikh's office supplies the missing answers
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. In the third item the questioner's whole difficulty is that Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib died during the fatrah, the interval between messengers, when — on the view the questioner assumes — no one is held accountable. The Sheikh affirms the hadith and does not address the fatrah at all. In the fifth item the questioner asks two things, and the bliss of women who never married is not answered. Nothing has been supplied for either. A reader who is not warned will take the answer given for an answer to the question asked.

flags.context: the third item as a whole
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). The fate of the Prophet's parents is one of the most contested questions in the tradition, and positions on it map onto live communal divisions. This answer takes a firm position on one side, in a few lines, without engaging the counter-arguments the questioner raises. It has been translated exactly as given, neither softened nor strengthened.

flags.arabic: و تعلق كل هذا حرام … و أما الحروز … فيمكن أن يعلق على المريض حتى يبرأ
flags.context: the second item, where two different objects receive two different rulings
options: keep amulets (tamāʾim) and written charms (ḥurūz) strictly distinct, as the Sheikh does
treat both under a single English term such as 'amulets'
flags.note: The whole force of this fatwa is the distinction between the two: tamāʾim are forbidden (ḥarām) and counted as shirk, while ḥurūz — Qur'anic or prophetic text, written whole and clean, for a specified illness, removed on recovery — may be hung. Collapsing the two terms into one English word would misattribute a ruling to the Sheikh in either direction. Note also the conditions he attaches: they are cumulative, and he rules that permanent wearing is 'of the work of the age of ignorance'.

flags.arabic: أنه ما من رجل من أهل الدنيا إلا و أقل نسائه في الجنة اثنتان من نساء الدنيا
options: translate as the Sheikh gives it, attributed as 'established from the Prophet' with no collection named
translate and note that no collection or grading is given
render as a statement of the Sheikh's own
flags.note: The Sheikh says ثبت عن النبي ('it is established from the Prophet') and gives the wording in quotation marks, but names no collection and no grading. He does give Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhari for the report of Ammar ibn Yasir later in the same item. The difference between the two attributions has been kept exactly, and nothing supplied for the first.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Five separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as five separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.
IMPORTANT FOR ANY LATER REVISION: in the fourth item wājib, jāʾiz and mustaḥīl carry the kalām senses required by style guide §8, not the five legal rulings. See the flag on that item.
The second item's question ends with an ellipsis in the source ('و الحروز؟...'), which has been reproduced; it is not a truncation introduced in extraction.
The Sheikh quotes five separate reports on amulets in the second item without naming a collection or grading for any of them. None has been supplied.

Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: رأىأحدا and برء وا written without or with a stray space, و ارأة فرعون for وامرأة فرعون, الحيواة for الحياة in the Qur'anic quotation (a Qur'anic orthography), يأيها for يا أيها, and the number shift in يزوجهن … فيختار لهما, where the plural and the dual are used of the same two women in one sentence.
